Weighted k-shell Degree Neighborhood Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch58.R
centrality_wksdn.Rd

The weighted k-shell degree neighborhood method (WKSDN; Maji 2020) gives every tie a weight built from the k-shell indices and degrees of its two ends, and scores a node by the weights of its ties: $$WKSDN(i) = \sum_{j \in N(i)} \bigl[(ks_i + ks_j) + \lambda (k_i + k_j)\bigr], \qquad \lambda = \frac{\sum_l ks_l}{\sum_l k_l}.$$

Usage

centrality_wksdn(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. \(\lambda\) is taken over the whole network, so adding a component can change every score. Isolated nodes score 0. The equations were taken from a later paper that reproduces them and from the Centrality Zoo; the 2020 article was not consulted, and no published value was available to check against. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Maji, G. (2020). Influential spreaders identification in complex networks with potential edge weight based k-shell degree neighborhood method. Journal of Computational Science, 39, 101055. doi:10.1016/j.jocs.2019.101055 .

See also

centrality_ink, centrality_coreness, centrality.

Examples

centrality_wksdn(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   78.51852   98.37037  119.70370   97.62963   77.77778   79.25926   61.62963 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   80.74074   99.11111   80.74074
